reason: E1 states Mo is a beta stabilizer with strong solid-solution strengthening in Ti alloys, but does not mention precipitation or nano-scale effects. E2 shows Mo addition to a different bcc HEA forms σ phase precipitates that improve 600°C strength, but the matrix is Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni, not Ti–Ni, and the precipitates are σ phase, not Mo-rich. The key premises about Mo-rich nano-precipitate formation in a Ti–Ni HEA and their specific strengthening mechanism are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Mo is a refractory element that provides strong solid-solution strengthening in Ti alloys
Mo addition to a bcc HEA can form nano-scale precipitates (e.g., σ phase) that contribute to high-temperature strength
A homogenization/aging treatment can induce Mo-rich nano-precipitates in a Ti–Ni HEA matrix
Mo-rich nano-precipitates will hinder dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at elevated temperatures
The proposed Mo addition and heat treatment will improve yield strength and creep resistance at 600–700°C
